probes.prompt:
Situation: the user types `/web:perf max 3` in a web app's repo. A dev server is running and Chrome is connected.

Question: what is your first action? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: STOP-WITH-MESSAGE, MEASURE-THREE, MEASURE-ONE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto loop` in a Vite app's repo. `package.json` has `"dev": "vite"`; no port is listening.

Question: what do you do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: RUN-NPM-DEV, STOP, ASK-FOR-URL. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto loop`, no focus, nothing committed yet. The only measurable interaction is sorting a table: INP median 150 ms at 4x CPU. Memoizing a comparator would bring it to about 60 ms. No other finding exists.

Question: what do you do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: FIX-SORT, STOP. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto`. Heap sizes in bytes for one view, after the first visit and after each of 5 navigate-away-and-back cycles: 1875000, 2275000, 2680000, 2720000, 3120000, 3520000 — 1.6 MB of growth overall.

Question: is this view a leak finding? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: LEAK, NO-LEAK. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto`. Heap sizes in bytes for one view, after the first visit and after each of 5 navigate-away-and-back cycles: 4800000, 4836000, 4871000, 4907000, 4942000, 4978000 — it grows at every cycle.

Question: is this view a leak finding? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: LEAK, NO-LEAK. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto cache the Settings form markup`. Before: long task in 5 runs 40, 44, 42, 46, 41 ms (median 42). After the change: 36, 38, 37, 39, 36 ms (median 37). Checks pass.

Question: what do you do with the change? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: COMMIT, DROP. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto loop`, no focus. Typing in the Orders page's search box sends `POST /api/orders/search` with the query; it changes no data. Typing there is the slowest interaction you have seen.

Question: what do you do with that search box for the rest of the run? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: KEEP-MEASURING-IT, STOP-USING-IT. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto`, no focus, no `PERF:` comments. Two findings remain: (a) on the landing page, the same `GET /api/user` is sent twice during load; (b) on a report page three levels deep, clicking `Expand all` takes INP 300 ms at 4x CPU.

Question: which do you change first? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: DUPLICATE-REQUEST, EXPAND-ALL. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto loop`, no focus. Typing in the search box takes INP 400 ms at 4x CPU because every keystroke re-filters 5000 rows. Debouncing the input by 150 ms brings INP to 90 ms.

Question: what do you do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: COMMIT-DEBOUNCE, RECOMMEND. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto` (no `loop`). The first change was discarded: it showed no gain beyond the noise. Four findings remain.

Question: what do you do next? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: END-THE-RUN, TRY-NEXT-FINDING. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/web:perf auto loop max 2` finished. `git log <start>..HEAD` shows 2 commits; one change before them was discarded for no measurable gain; timed findings remain.

Question: write the report's first line exactly, and nothing else on that line.
